hops.title: Compare it: five crayons versus a giant box
hops.text: Hand your child just five crayons and ask what a kitchen drawing looks like with only five colours. Your tongue works with a short set too: five basic tastes. Your nose carries nearly four hundred kinds of smell sensors. Together, they turn plain sweet or sour into full flavour.

sources.citation: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD), NIH, 'Taste Disorders'
Niimura, Y. & Nei, M. (2003), 'Evolution of olfactory receptor genes in the human genome', PNAS 100(21):12235-12240
National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD), NIH, 'Smell Disorders'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: Two smiling children at a wooden kitchen table look at a small box of five crayons beside a huge open box of hundreds of crayons.
image.caption: Five basic tastes team up with nearly four hundred kinds of smell sensors to make full flavour.

hops.title: Say it: wave smells like a snake flicks its tongue
hops.text: "A snake flicks its forked tongue to scoop tiny smell specks out of the air. A gentle wave of your hand sends smell specks to your nose!" Use this right when you show your child how to waft over a covered cup instead of pressing a nose against the foil.

sources.citation: National Park Service, Upper Delaware Scenic & Recreational River, 'Snakes'
National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD), NIH, 'Smell Disorders'

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A small green garter snake on a mossy stone flicking its forked tongue toward tiny drifting particles in the air.
image.caption: Snakes flick their forked tongues to gather tiny smell specks; we wave them toward our nose instead.

hops.afterHeading: Questions to ask while you do it
hops.title: Ask it: whose nose would you borrow for a day?
hops.text: Ask your child, "If you could borrow any animal's nose for a day, whose would you pick?" Expect playful answers like a dog, bear, or shark. Celebrate their pick, then share a surprise: African savanna elephants have about two thousand kinds of smell sensors, roughly five times ours. Ask what an elephant might sniff first.

sources.citation: Niimura, Y., Matsui, A. & Touhara, K. (2014), 'Extreme expansion of the olfactory receptor gene repertoire in African elephants and evolutionary dynamics of orthologous gene groups in 13 placental mammals', Genome Research 24(9):1485-1496
Niimura, Y. & Nei, M. (2003), 'Evolution of olfactory receptor genes in the human genome', PNAS 100(21):12235-12240

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: An African savanna elephant lifting its trunk toward leaves and wildflowers to sniff the breeze.
image.caption: African savanna elephants have about two thousand kinds of smell sensors, roughly five times our number.
